claims.text: Fabric Mirroring is a fully managed, serverless replication service that continuously brings data from external operational and analytical databases into OneLake, converting it to Parquet files in Delta Lake format, without requiring users to build or maintain ETL pipelines.

Fabric supports three distinct mirroring approaches: database mirroring (physically replicates table data), metadata mirroring (synchronizes only catalog structure via OneLake shortcuts, leaving data in place), and open mirroring (allows any developer to write change data directly to a mirrored database item via public APIs and a landing zone URL).

The supported database mirroring sources (GA or preview as of June 2026) include Azure Cosmos DB, Azure SQL Database, Azure SQL Managed Instance, Azure Database for PostgreSQL, Azure Database for MySQL (preview), SQL Server, Snowflake, Oracle, SAP, Google BigQuery (preview), Fabric SQL database (auto-configured), and open mirrored databases. Azure Databricks is supported via metadata mirroring and Dremio via metadata mirroring (preview).

For database and open mirroring, the internal replicator engine polls a Fabric landing zone at high frequency and immediately merges incremental Delta files into the target Delta table; changes from the source can propagate into OneLake in as little as 15 seconds under optimal conditions.

Metadata mirroring does not move or copy data — it only synchronizes catalog names, schemas, and table definitions, using OneLake shortcuts to point at the source data in place. As a result, latency for metadata mirroring is governed by source system access time and shortcut performance, not by a data-copy pipeline.

The replication engine employs backoff logic that scales down polling frequency when source activity is low, reducing overhead on the source database engine and adjusting automatically when change volume rises again.

Mirroring storage for replicated data is free up to one terabyte per capacity unit (CU) purchased. An F64 capacity therefore includes 64 TB of free mirroring storage exclusively for replicas; charges apply if that limit is exceeded or when the Fabric capacity is paused.

Background compute used by the mirroring replication process itself is free and does not consume Fabric capacity units. Standard capacity consumption applies to downstream analytical workloads — querying via SQL, Power BI, or Spark — that access the mirrored data in OneLake.

Because mirrored data lands in Delta Lake format in OneLake, Power BI semantic models can connect to it using Direct Lake mode, enabling near-real-time reporting on operational data without importing or duplicating the data into the model.

Cross-database T-SQL queries can span mirrored databases, Fabric warehouses, and lakehouse SQL analytics endpoints in a single statement using standard three-part naming, because all of these item types expose data through OneLake.

Metadata mirroring supports cross-tenant data sharing through OneLake external data sharing: a read-only shortcut is created in the consumer tenant, allowing both organizations to query the same live source data without duplication or additional ETL.

Mirroring automatically runs vacuum on Delta tables to remove files no longer referenced in the Delta log. The default retention period is one day for databases created after mid-June 2025 (seven days for older databases) and can be adjusted via the Fabric portal or the public REST API to balance storage cost against Delta time-travel range.
